text: Age: 59
Occupation: Retired Commerce Employee

Hello, My name is Nick Padilla, was born and raised in Commerce, attended Bandini Elementary, Bell Gardens High school, and received AA degree at Cerritos College. Taking courses in management, Landscape architecture ROP program with the City of Commerce, learning and beautifying the city's parks and outdoor facilities. I was hired Full time in 1985 with the City of Commerce as Park Maintenance Worker and moved up in various positions beautifying our parks, facilities, and city medians. I retired in 2025 after 40 years of service. If elected City Council Member, I will do my very best to bring back the "The Model City" by:

- Strong on Crime, Improve Public Safety, having city security Patrol all residential streets and parks every day and night as they did in the past.
- Bring back our Neighborhood watch program, with block captains as it was in past
- Support Senior services and programs.
- Evaluate safety and improve parking issues.
- Open up snack bar in the Heart of our city, Rosewood park.
- Stabilize city revenue, bring in grocery market & other restaurants, stores, not be dependent upon one main revenue producer like the casino
- Beautification of city parks, facilities, medians, streets, alleys, making our city "clean and green!"
- Work hard to produce education programs and jobs for city residents.

text: Occupation: Advanced Automotive Technician
Commerce is my lifelong home, the community that raised me, and where my family's story continues.

I'm Jaime Valencia. My wife Claudia and I have been married for 10 years, and I help care for my elderly parents, who also call Commerce home. I want Commerce to remain a place where families feel safe, supported, and proud to stay for generations.

I had the privilege of working as a Commerce lifeguard and later serving as a Planning Commissioner and Education Commissioner. I have also served as President of the Commerce Lions Club and volunteered to improve our neighborhoods.
After 30 years as an accountant, I became an advanced-certified automotive technician. Both careers taught me to examine details, solve problems responsibly, and consider how decisions affect people.

I am running for City Council because residents deserve a government that listens, responds, and earns their trust. My priorities include addressing vehicle theft and illegal fireworks, strengthening programs for families and seniors, promoting responsible development, protecting taxpayer dollars, and moving forward with the redevelopment of Veterans Park.
I respectfully ask for your trust, your vote, and the opportunity to serve you on the Commerce City Council.

text: Age: 58
Occupation: Mayor Pro Tem
Friends,

strong: I am excited to serve as your Mayor Pro Tem and once again seek your vote.

text: Over the past term, my top priority has been the well-being of the residents who call our city home. I have always believed that a thriving community begins with a simple, foundational promise:

strong: every neighborhood must be safe, and every family must have the support they need to succeed.

text: During my tenure, we have successfully delivered several key initiatives and capital projects to uplift our community:
Established the Bandini Learning Center and expanded community arts programs.
Implemented administrative changes to improve public safety, enhanced traffic control measures, and upgraded the walkways at Rosewood Park.
Honored our military families by hosting the America's Freedom Tribute & Traveling Vietnam Memorial Wall and completed extensive cleanups of street medians and rights-of-way.
Approved a new replacement structure for local sports activities and secured vital economic revenue by passing a progressive digital billboard ordinance.
There is still important work to do. I ask for your continued support to keep moving forward together—with safe streets, strong neighborhoods, and families first.
Respectfully, Mireya Garcia

text: Age: 44
Occupation: Mayor

The City of Commerce is where I proudly chose to raise my family, and serving our community has been such an honor. Four years ago, I ran for City Council because our City faced unprecedented challenges. The pandemic shut down programs, delayed projects, strained our budget, and tested our sense of community.

Together, we've made real progress. I've worked to improve roads and sidewalks, upgrade our parks, support economic development, expand rental assistance for seniors and veterans, launch free Wi-Fi at our parks and facilities, enhance youth and senior services, strengthen our home beautification programs, and adopt smarter building standards for City facilities that save energy and reduce long-term costs.

While I'm proud of what we've accomplished, our work isn't finished. We must continue making Commerce safer, supporting small businesses, creating new housing and economic opportunities, revitalizing underused City properties, and keeping our neighborhoods clean and well maintained.

Commerce deserves ethical leadership that delivers results while planning for the future. That is the standard I've worked to uphold every day I've had the privilege of serving you. I would be honored to earn your support so we can continue moving Commerce forward together.

text: Age: 44
Occupation: Senior Quality Engineer
My name is Vanessa Haro and I am running for City of Commerce city council to bring a community-first focused perspective, where the residents' voice, health and safety are top priority.

I am a fourth-generation Commerce resident and grew up participating in many of Commerce's opportunities, including sports, swim lessons, Miss Commerce and Washington DC trips. I run a non-profit karate dojo out of the St. Marcellinus Church in Commerce where I have the honor of training many of our residents and was honored on the Commerce Wall of Champions.

I plan is to be a consistent advocate for the residents. My focus includes addressing and getting ahead of any chemical, or hazardous issues that can threaten our community. I plan to bring financial resources to the community to help us keep our homes and investments and bring new resources and opportunity to legacy residents wanting to purchase homes in Commerce.

Our community is the reason Commerce is the model city. I want the physical and financial health of our residents and businesses to flourish and thrive in Commerce, while preserving our tight-knit community and bringing back the legacy programs and clubs that originally made us the model city.
